taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes American ranid genus arrangements are contested (Lithobates vs Rana); the batch name follows NatureServe's Lithobates. Older literature refers to it as Rana pipiens.
fieldMarks: Never green; usually a distinct pale spot on the eardrum
Posterior end of the dorsolateral ridges inset or angled inward
Light line along the upper jaw and a dark snout spot (per Animal Diversity Web)
Yellow on the groin and underside of the thigh (per Animal Diversity Web)
behavior: Males call from the water surface; call of 2-3 distinct 'chucks' (Animal Diversity Web)
Lays eggs in spring, summer or early fall, often after heavy rain
Burrows into mud in winter; some move up to 8 km between ponds
habitat: Streams, ponds, ditches and marshes in prairie, desert grassland and farmland; may range into surrounding land in wet weather.
range: Southern South Dakota to central Texas, west to eastern Colorado and eastern New Mexico, east to Indiana and southeastern Missouri; disjunct in southeastern Arizona. Hybridizes with northern leopard frog in eastern Colorado and Nebraska. Not a Canadian species.

lookalikes.name: Northern leopard frog
lookalikes.howToTell: Can be green, usually lacks the pale eardrum spot, ridges not inset at the rear.
